articles.title: Solitaire(ish) turns classic card stacking into a roguelike for Apple Arcade
articles.summary: solitaire(ish) is the new one from Playstack, the publisher behind Balatro, and it’s coming to Apple Arcade next month. So, Solitaire. But a roguelike, and made in-house at Playstack Leeds. There’s a boss too, a King, and he’s allowed to change the rules on you whenever he likes (reverse stacking included, which sounds properly nasty). Most of it you’ll already know. Descending order, red on black, black on red, same as ever. Now every stack scores, though, and there’s a target to hit that keeps climbing each round. You earn cash along the way and spend it in the shop, where Switchers are the simple option, letting you swap the rank or colour of a card that’s already down. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: The Red Cathedral brings its competitive cathedral-building board game to iOS and Android
articles.summary: It’s been a little while coming, but Devir’s digital edition of The Red Cathedral is finally out on iOS and Android (and on PC through Steam, for that matter). I wrote about it back when it was first announced in May, and Iwan had another look in September once it got a release date, so we’ve been keeping tabs on this one for most of the year. You’re after the Tsar’s favour - Ivan the Terrible, no less, and so is everyone else at the table. Up to four of you are chipping in on the same cathedral, though each of you has claimed your own bits of it, and you need to go and find the materials to actually build those bits and then decorate them. The clergy and the city’s guilds come into it too. Whoever’s racked up the most prestige by the time the whole thing is finished wins. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: The Sunday Papers
articles.summary: While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist. Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose? Read more
